blocks.title: Microscopic events
blocks.text: Microscopic events are the phenomena that cannot be observed with the naked eye.
The collisions between molecules, the breaking and forming of bonds, the rearrangement of atoms in molecules, and the loss or gain of electrons are examples of microscopic events.

blocks.prompt: Differentiate between macroscopic and microscopic events, giving one example of each from the burning of magnesium.
blocks.explanation: Macroscopic events are visible: magnesium burns with a bright white flame, gives out heat and leaves a white powder. Microscopic events are invisible: magnesium atoms lose electrons to oxygen atoms, bonds in O2 break and new Mg-O bonds form. The visible changes are the sum of countless invisible ones.

items: Microscopic events cannot be seen: molecular collisions, bond breaking and forming, rearrangement of atoms, loss or gain of electrons.
